arxiv-2011-13894.title: Efficient Scene Compression for Visual-based Localization
arxiv-2011-13894.creator: Marcela Mera-Trujillo, Benjamin Smith, Victor Fragoso
arxiv-2011-13894.description: Abstract Estimating the pose of a camera with respect to a 3D reconstruction or scene representation is a crucial step for many mixed reality and robotics applications. Given the vast amount of available data nowadays, many applications constrain storage and/or bandwidth to work efficiently.

arxiv-2104-10412.title: Comprehensive Multi-Modal Interactions for Referring Image Segmentation
arxiv-2104-10412.creator: Kanishk Jain, Vineet Gandhi
arxiv-2104-10412.description: Abstract We investigate Referring Image Segmentation (RIS), which outputs a segmentation map corresponding to the natural language description. Addressing RIS efficiently requires considering the interactions happening across visual and linguistic modalities and the interactions within each modality. Existing methods are limited because they either compute different forms of interactions sequentially (leading to error propagation) or ignore intramodal interactions.

arxiv-2310-19775.title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) 2.0: A Manifesto of Open Challenges and Interdisciplinary Research Directions
arxiv-2310-19775.creator: Luca Longo, Mario Brcic, Federico Cabitza, Jaesik Choi, Roberto Confalonieri, Javier Del Ser, Riccardo Guidotti, Yoichi Hayashi, Francisco Herrera, Andreas Holzinger, Richard Jiang, Hassan Khosravi, Freddy Lecue, Gianclaudio Malgieri, Andrés Páez, Wojciech Samek, Johannes Schneider, Timo Speith, Sim
arxiv-2310-19775.description: Abstract As systems based on opaque AI ( AI ) continue to flourish in diverse real-world applications, understanding these black box models has become paramount. In response, XAI ( XAI ) has emerged as a field of research with practical and ethical benefits across various domains.

arxiv-2401-10867.title: Learning Optimal Dynamic Treatment Regimes from Longitudinal Data
arxiv-2401-10867.creator: Nicholas T. Williams, MPH, Katherine L. Hoffman, MS, Iván Díaz, PhD, Kara E. Rudolph, PhD
arxiv-2401-10867.description: Abstract Studies often report estimates of the average treatment effect (ATE). While the ATE summarizes the effect of a treatment on average, it does not provide any information about the effect of treatment within any individual. A treatment strategy that uses an individual’s information to tailor treatment to maximize benefit is known as an optimal dynamic treatment rule (ODTR).

arxiv-2501-07138.title: Asymptotics for some q q -hypergeometric polynomials
arxiv-2501-07138.creator: Juan F. Mañas–Mañas, Juan J. Moreno–Balcázar
arxiv-2501-07138.description: Abstract We tackle the study of a type of local asymptotics, known as Mehler–Heine asymptotics, for some q q –hypergeometric polynomials. Some consequences about the asymptotic behavior of the zeros of these polynomials are discussed. We illustrate the results with numerical examples. a Departamento de Matemáticas, Universidad de Almería, Spain. b Instituto Carlos I de Física Teórica y Computacional, Spain.

arxiv-2504-20662.title: On the Optimal Source Key Size of Secure Gradient Coding
arxiv-2504-20662.creator: Yang Zhou, Wenbo Huang, Kai Wan, Robert Caiming Qiu, Claude E. Shannon and David Slepian, Yang Zhou 1 , Wenbo Huang 1 † , Kai Wan 1 , Robert Caiming Qiu 1
arxiv-2504-20662.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yang Zhou, Wenbo Huang, Kai Wan, Robert Caiming Qiu, Claude E. Shannon and David Slepian, Yang Zhou 1 , Wenbo Huang 1 † , Kai Wan 1 , Robert Caiming Qiu 1. Gradient coding enables a user node to efficiently aggregate gradients computed by server nodes from local datasets, achieving low communication costs while ensuring resilience against straggling servers.

arxiv-2510-13515.title: UniME-V2: MLLM-as-a-Judge for Universal Multimodal Embedding Learning
arxiv-2510-13515.creator: Tiancheng Gu, Kaicheng Yang, Kaichen Zhang, Xiang An, Ziyong Feng, Yueyi Zhang, Weidong Cai, Jiankang Deng, Lidong Bing
arxiv-2510-13515.description: Abstract Universal multimodal embedding models are foundational to various tasks. Existing approaches typically employ in-batch negative mining by measuring the similarity of query-candidate pairs. However, these methods often struggle to capture subtle semantic differences among candidates and lack diversity in negative samples. Moreover, the embeddings exhibit limited discriminative ability in distinguishing false and hard negatives.

arxiv-2601-17662.title: From Joint to Single-System ψ \psi -Onticity Without Preparation Independence
arxiv-2601-17662.creator: Shan Gao
arxiv-2601-17662.description: Abstract The Pusey–Barrett–Rudolph (PBR) theorem establishes ψ \psi -onticity for individual quantum systems, but its standard formulation relies on the Preparation Independence Postulate (PIP). This has led to a prevalent view that rejecting PIP leaves open the possibility of ψ \psi -epistemic models for individual systems.

plos-pone-0001950.creator: Caroline Charlier, Françoise Dromer, Christophe Lévêque et al.
plos-pone-0001950.description: PLOS ONE research article. Cryptococcal meningoencephalitis has an overall global mortality rate of 20% in AIDS patients despite antifungals. There is a need for additional means of precise assessment of disease severity. We thus studied the radiological brain images available from 62 HIV-positive patients

pmc-10656516.title: Patterning and dynamics of membrane adhesion under hydraulic stress
pmc-10656516.creator: Céline Dinet, Alejandro Torres-Sánchez, Roberta Lanfranco, Lorenzo Di Michele, Marino Arroyo, Margarita Staykova
pmc-10656516.description: Hydraulic fracturing plays a major role in cavity formation during embryonic development, when pressurized fluid opens microlumens at cell-cell contacts, which evolve to form a single large lumen. However, the fundamental physical mechanisms behind these processes remain masked by the complexity and specificity of biological systems.

pmc-10736654.title: OUT OF THE MEDICINE CABINET: NONPHARMACOLOGICAL APPROACHES TO IMPROVE COGNITION AND ASSOCIATED FUNCTIONS
pmc-10736654.creator: Ashley Curtis, Constance Visovsky
pmc-10736654.description: There is a lack of pharmacological agents for improving cognition, and the negative impact of polypharmacy on cognitive and physiological functioning in aging adults is well established. This has prompted investigation of non-pharmacological interventions aimed at improving cognition and associated functions. This symposium will provide a comprehensive evaluation of several of these promising evidence-based behavioral approaches.

pmc-11367617.title: Model-based navigation of transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation in humans: Application to targeting the amygdala and thalamus
pmc-11367617.creator: Mohammad Daneshzand, Bastien Guerin, Parker Kotlarz, Tina Chou, Darin D. Dougherty, Brian L. Edlow, Aapo Nummenmaa
pmc-11367617.description: Background:Transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) neuromodulation has shown promise in animals but is challenging to translate to humans because of the thicker skull that heavily scatters ultrasound waves.Objective:We develop and disseminate a model-based navigation (MBN) tool for acoustic dose delivery in the presence of skull aberrations that is easy to use by non-specialists.

pmc-11575634.title: Synergistic global and local flexibilities in Zr-based metal–organic frameworks enable sequential sieving of hexane isomers†
pmc-11575634.creator: Rundao Chen, Jiaqi Li, Fang Zheng, Fangru Zhou, Bin Sheng, Baojian Liu, Qiwei Yang, Zhiguo Zhang, Qilong Ren, Zongbi Bao
pmc-11575634.description: Separating hexane isomers based on the branching degree is crucial for their efficient utilization in the petrochemical industry, yet remains challenging due to their similar properties. Here we report a temperature-responsive Zr-based metal–organic framework, Zr-fum-FA, capable of sequentially sieving linear, mono-, and di-branched hexane isomers.

pmc-11608639.creator: Ross I. S. Zbar, Lisa D. Taylor, John W. Canady
pmc-11608639.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). e to patient dissatisfaction if not addressed. Drivers of dissatisfaction after breast reduction surgery typically include poor scarring, persistent ptosis, or wound breakdown.2,3 However, some patients also express concern over the continued prominence of the subaxillary region.4 Although articles on breast reduction techniques rarely discuss the subaxillary fat pad, many surgeons address this area with liposuction to enhance postoperative satisfaction and maintain a competitive edge.5 The proliferation of social media has led to a misconception that addressing the subaxillary fat pad is

pmc-11644644.title: Genome-Wide Approach of Gene–Nutrient Intake Interaction Study for Essential Hypertension in a Large Korean Cohort (KoGES)
pmc-11644644.creator: Youhyun Song, Ja-Eun Choi, Jae-Min Park, Yu-Jin Kwon, Kyung-Won Hong, Ji-Won Lee
pmc-11644644.description: Background/Objectives: There is limited evidence on gene-nutrient interaction associated with hypertension (HTN). We examined interactions between genotypes and various nutrients that influenced high blood pressure (BP). Methods: Data were obtained from a total of 50,808 participants from the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study (KoGES). Dietary intake was assessed by a food frequency questionnaire, and dietary reference intakes (DRIs) were set.

pmc-11716727.title: Effects of APOE genotype on cortical atrophy in early onset Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11716727.creator: Diane Chan, Michael Brickhouse, Alexander Zaitsev, Bonnie Wong, Dustin B Hammers, Jeffrey L Dage, Tatiana M Foroud, Ani Eloyan, Kelly N Nudelman, Sára Nemes, Maria C Carrillo, Gil D Rabinovici, Liana G Apostolova, Bradford C Dickerson, Alexandra Touroutoglou, the LEADS Consortium
pmc-11716727.description: BackgroundAPOE‐ɛ4 is a major risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD); its effects have been examined in late‐onset AD (LOAD) but less so in early‐onset AD (EOAD). In LOAD, APOE genotype has strong effects on episodic memory and medial temporal lobe (MTL) atrophy (Wolk & Dickerson, 2010).

pmc-12602267.title: Endovascular treatment of unruptured intracranial aneurysms at a single center: Outcomes, selection strategy, and transparent communication for patient decision-making
pmc-12602267.creator: Gianmarco Bernava, Abiram Sandralegar, Jeremy Hofmeister, Andrea Rosi, Hasan Yilmaz, Sandrine Morel, Philippe Reymond, Olivier Brina, Michel Muster, Karl-Olof Lovblad, Karl Schaller, Philippe Bijlenga, Paolo Machi
pmc-12602267.description: BackgroundThe management of unruptured intracranial aneurysms (UIA) requires a balance between procedural risks and the potential benefit of rupture prevention.ObjectiveThe aim of this study is to evaluate the clinical and anatomical results of endovascular treatment for UIAs at our institution, to benchmark our practice and potential areas for improvement, and enable transparent communication with patients by providing accurate, evidence-based information.

pmc-12691021.title: Examining Health-Related Quality of Life in Cancer Survivors: Cross-Sectional Associations with Comorbidities, Navigation Services Use, and Perceived Social Support
pmc-12691021.creator: Daniela López-Vallejo, Cynthia M Pérez, Lorena González-Sepúlveda, Marievelisse Soto-Salgado, Eduardo Nagore
pmc-12691021.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryWhile cancer survivors are living longer, many also face ongoing chronic health conditions that reduce their quality of life. These chronic conditions are common but remain understudied in cancer survivors, particularly in Puerto Rico. This study examined the association between comorbidity burden and health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and whether support services, such as patient navigation or perceived social support, modify this association.

pmc-12821172.title: Role of LINC00332 in colorectal cancer progression and paclitaxel resistance
pmc-12821172.creator: Meysam Moghbeli, Negin Taghehchian, Mahsa Palizkaran Yazdi, Mohammad Reza Abbaszadegan
pmc-12821172.description: BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer and a leading cause of cancer deaths. Standard therapeutic management is faced with challenges like treatment resistance and late-stage diagnosis, highlighting a need for better diagnosis. LncRNAs are crucial in CRC progression and may serve as non-invasive biomarkers.

pmc-13119533.title: A Sensitive Multichannel Fluorescent Polymer Sensor Array for the Detection of Protein Fluctuations in Serum
pmc-13119533.creator: Junwhee Yang, Colby Alves, Kanwal Nazir, Mingdi Jiang, Nicolas Araujo, Vincent M. Rotello
pmc-13119533.description: Serum contains diverse proteins whose concentrations vary with pathological conditions such as cancer, liver disease, neurological disorder, and infections. Conventional methods like serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) are gold standards for protein identification; however, they are time-consuming and can miss abnormal serum protein levels.

pmc-13139232.title: Endoscopic treatment versus open excision for pediatric pilonidal disease: technical description of a modified (P)EPSiT approach using standard equipment and retrospective cohort study
pmc-13139232.creator: J Kirsch, S Drossard, K Schriek, U Hübner
pmc-13139232.description: BackgroundEndoscopic pilonidal sinus treatment (EPSiT) has emerged as a minimally invasive treatment option for pilonidal disease (PD) in adolescents, yet its adoption has been limited by the need for specialized equipment. We developed a modified EPSiT technique using standard urological instruments, saline irrigation, and lateral positioning, which was introduced in 2019.
